_doc: HMTc Category 2 (Infant and Child Personal Care, ages 0-5) compiler config. Method v2.0, government-limit default: every number is a REGULATORY LOOKUP against a named row of data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, never an occurrence calculation. The governing instrument family is sovereign COSMETIC contaminant law, which limits heavy metals as technically unavoidable impurities in the FINISHED product on a TOTAL-CONTENT basis (ug/kg of product as placed on market). That is never a dietary basis and never a migration or leachate basis, and the basis guard on every row enforces it. The binding instrument across the category is Germany's BVL 2017 table of technically avoidable heavy-metal contents, which is the strictest general-cosmetic tier in the register for lead, cadmium, total arsenic and total mercury, and the only instrument that publishes a separate stricter TOOTHPASTE tier; Korea MFDS is the only sovereign that limits nickel in a finished cosmetic. Five of the eleven panel cells - inorganic arsenic, tin, aluminium, total chromium and hexavalent chromium - have no sovereign finished-cosmetic maximum anywhere in the register and are published as CONTROLS rather than as invented ceilings. Methylmercury is the category's single not-material determination, speciation-bounded by total mercury. See _category.method_note for the three category-specific rules (child floor-plus, swallowed-product tier, mineral splits) that govern every row.

_category.name: Infant and Child Personal Care (Ages 0-5)
_category.anchor: strictest sovereign finished-cosmetic technically-unavoidable-impurity limit on a total-content basis, with the swallowed-product (toothpaste) tier read across to the ingestion-adjacent oral forms and every adult-market loosening carve-out declined for a 0-5 product
_category.basis_family: finished cosmetic product as placed on market, total heavy-metal content in ug/kg; never a migration or leachate basis, never a colour-additive or raw-material purity specification, never a dietary basis
_category.method_label: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default) as applied to a child-scoped cosmetic category: every numeric cell is the strictest applicable sovereign finished-cosmetic maximum in the row's native total-content basis, or a disclosed read-across of a stricter sovereign tier from the same instrument where that instrument writes an adult-market loosening carve-out that HMTc declines to adopt for a product marketed to ages 0-5. No cell is occurrence-derived.
_category.method_note:
Category 2 is the child-scoped personal-care category (ages 0-5). Three category-specific rules govern every row and are stated here once.

RULE 1 - THE CHILD ROW IS A FLOOR-PLUS, NEVER A DISCOUNT. Category 13 (adult leave-on cosmetics) and Category 14 (adult rinse-off cosmetics) cover the same product forms for adults. A Category 2 row is never looser than the Category 13/14 row for the same form. Where a sovereign instrument publishes a CHILD-scoped tier, that tier is the applicable cell. Where it publishes an ADULT-market loosening carve-out, Category 2 does not adopt it. Two such carve-outs bind in practice. Germany's BVL 2017 raises lead from 2.0 to 5.0 mg/kg for make-up powder, rouge, eye shadow, eyeliner, kajal and theatrical, fan or carnival make-up, and raises arsenic from 0.5 to 2.5 mg/kg for theatrical, fan or carnival make-up; Korea's MFDS raises nickel from 10 to 30 ug/g for colour cosmetics and 35 ug/g for eye make-up. Both carve-outs exist because adult decorative cosmetics carry heavy pigment loads. Neither is a child determination. A children's face paint or play make-up is applied to a 0-5 child's face, transferred hand-to-mouth and licked; certifying it at five times the general cosmetic lead limit would be indefensible. Those rows therefore read across the SAME instrument's general-cosmetic tier, which is stricter, and the refused carve-out is named in the cell so the reader can see exactly what was declined and why. This is over-compliance against a real sovereign number, not an invented one; Category 16 (Supplements, live) set the same precedent by applying the strictest child-protective limit across an entire category.

RULE 2 - THE INGESTION-ADJACENT ORAL FORMS TAKE THE SWALLOWED-PRODUCT TIER. Germany's BVL 2017 is the only instrument in the register that publishes a separate, stricter TOOTHPASTE tier (lead 0.5 mg/kg against 2.0 mg/kg general). That tier exists because toothpaste sits on the oral mucosa and is partly swallowed. Children's toothpaste binds it directly. Children's lip balm reads across it: a lip product on a 0-5 child is applied to the vermilion border, contacts the oral mucosa and is swallowed at a fraction at least comparable to toothpaste, and the swallowed-product tier is the nearest sovereign cell for that pathway. Category 15 (Feminine Care, live) established this read-across pattern by taking the BVL toothpaste tier onto mucosal-contact products. Face paint, children's make-up and nail polish do NOT take the toothpaste tier: hand-to-mouth transfer from those forms is incidental contamination, not the product's designed contact surface, and stretching an oral-mucosal tier onto skin-applied decorative cosmetics would be a distinction the instrument does not draw.

RULE 3 - THE MINERAL SPLITS ARE REAL BUT THEY DO NOT MOVE THE NUMBER. The taxonomy splits four pairs on mineral content: cornstarch versus talc baby powder, chemical versus mineral baby sunscreen, non-ZnO versus ZnO diaper cream, and plain versus mineral-bearing children's lip balm. The split is correct: talc, zinc oxide, titanium dioxide, mica and iron oxides are the raw materials that carry the metal load, so the two halves of each pair have entirely different contamination risk profiles and must be sampled and qualified differently. But the split does NOT produce two different sovereign numbers, and this standard does not manufacture one. The only mineral-specific tiers in the register are LOOSENINGS: the EAEU TR CU 009/2011 tier for perfumery-cosmetic products containing more than 1% natural plant or natural mineral raw material sets lead at 5.0 mg/kg, arsenic at 5.0 mg/kg and mercury at 1.0 mg/kg, and Korea's MFDS raises lead to 50 ug/g for powder products using clay as a raw material. Every one of those values is looser than the general cosmetic tier this standard binds, and none is adopted for a 0-5 product. The mineral rows therefore bind the same ceilings as their clean counterparts, which makes them harder to meet, which is the intended and honest outcome. What the mineral rows add is a raw-material qualification obligation carried in the row's scope note, not a different number.

WHAT THE REGISTER DOES NOT SUPPORT. Five of the eleven panel cells have no sovereign finished-cosmetic maximum anywhere in the register and are published as CONTROLS rather than as invented ceilings: inorganic arsenic (no jurisdiction speciates arsenic in a cosmetic; bounded by the binding total-arsenic ceiling), tin, aluminium, total chromium and hexavalent chromium. The only hexavalent-chromium number in the cosmetic instrument family is EU REACH entry 2020/2081 at 500 ug/kg, which is scoped to mixtures injected intradermally for tattooing and permanent make-up - a different exposure route, a different product class and a different risk basis - and it is not read across onto surface-applied children's cosmetics. The only total-chromium, tin and aluminium numbers are EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48 and ASTM F963 element-MIGRATION limits, which are numerically incomparable to a total-content cosmetic limit. Control is the correct fail-safe for all five: testing is mandatory, the analytical method and the escalation rule are published, and no ceiling is fabricated.

REGISTER GAP OF RECORD. Sri Lanka SLS 187:2025 is the only CHILD-scoped cosmetic instrument in the register (skin powder for children, talc-base and starch-base). Every one of its rows carries status 'draft guidance; not for implementation' and is gated out by the compiler, so it anchors nothing here. Its published values (lead 10 mg/kg, cadmium 3 mg/kg, arsenic 1.5 mg/kg, mercury 1 mg/kg) are in every case LOOSER than the German BVL general-cosmetic tier this standard binds, so no protection is lost by its exclusion; it is recorded as a register gap for verified re-ingest, not as a missed stricter anchor. The US FDA draft cosmetic lead guidance (10 mg/kg) is gated for the same reason and is likewise looser.
_category.credible_note: The default HMTc credible-regulator set (EU, UK, Codex, international, US, AU-NZ, CA, HK) is written for FOOD instruments and contains almost no cosmetic contaminant law: the EU regulates cosmetic heavy metals through Regulation 1223/2009 Annex II, which prohibits lead, cadmium, mercury and arsenic compounds as ingredients but publishes no numeric trace ceiling, and Codex has no cosmetic mandate at all. The sovereign instruments that DO set finished-cosmetic contaminant maxima are national: Germany (BVL 2017), Health Canada, US FDA (21 CFR 700.13), Washington State (Toxic-Free Cosmetics Act), China (NMPA 2015), Korea (MFDS), Taiwan (MOHW 2024), Hong Kong (Cap. 640), Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive, India, Kenya, the EAEU, Australia, New Zealand, Brazil and Sri Lanka. The credible set is widened to those jurisdictions so that (a) the strictest applicable value can actually be found and (b) the compiler's stricter-unselected audit scan can see every sovereign row that could embarrass a published binding. Widening the set makes the audit STRICTER, not looser: it can only surface more candidate anchors, never fewer. Germany's BVL 2017 table is admitted as a sovereign instrument because it is issued by a German federal authority and operationalises the Article 17 'technically unavoidable' test that EU Regulation 1223/2009 makes binding law; the Category 15 (Feminine Care) standard, live since 2026-08-17, already rests on it.

baby-lotion-cream.name: Baby lotion and cream
baby-lotion-cream.native_basis: finished cosmetic product as placed on the market — total heavy-metal content per unit mass of the product as sold (ug/kg). Total content, never a migration or leachate number, never a colour-additive or raw-material purity specification, and never a dietary basis.
baby-lotion-cream.native_basis_label: finished cosmetic as placed on market (total content, ug/kg of product as sold)
baby-lotion-cream.scope_note: Leave-on emulsions (oil-in-water and water-in-oil lotions, creams and balms) marketed for ages 0-5 and applied to intact skin without rinsing. In scope regardless of whether the product is sold as a moisturiser, massage cream or after-bath cream. OUT of scope: diaper creams, which route to the two diaper-cream rows because the application site is occluded and macerated; sunscreens, which route to the two baby-sunscreen rows because UV-filter minerals change the raw-material risk; and adult leave-on cosmetics, which route to Category 13. Taxonomy boundary rule: a leave-on baby product marketed for ages 0-5 routes here and not to Category 13, because infant dermal exposure assumptions - thinner stratum corneum, higher surface-area-to-mass ratio, hand-to-mouth transfer - differ from the adult case.
baby-lotion-cream.basis_guard_note: Every named anchor must carry a FINISHED-COSMETIC basis. The guard exists to keep three foreign bases out of these cells: (1) the 21 CFR 73/74 colour-additive ingredient specifications, which are purity limits for one raw material (iron oxides, ultramarines, henna, bismuth citrate, talc-bearing pigments) and not a ceiling on the finished product; (2) the EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48 and ASTM F963 element-MIGRATION limits, which measure what leaches out of an article and are numerically incomparable to a total-content limit; and (3) food maximum levels expressed as-consumed or on an edible-portion basis. A cell whose named anchor fails the guard resolves to a GAP and fails the build rather than shipping a conflated number.

Pb.label: strictest applicable sovereign finished-cosmetic lead limit (Germany BVL 2017 Table 1, technically avoidable heavy-metal contents)
Pb.basis_label: finished cosmetic as placed on market (total content, ug/kg of product as sold)
Pb.substantiation: Germany's BVL 2017 Table 1 is the strictest sovereign finished-cosmetic lead limit in the register at 2.0 mg/kg, roughly five times stricter than Health Canada (10 mg/kg), China NMPA 2015 (10 mg/kg) and Taiwan MOHW 2024 (10 mg/kg), which are named alongside it so the derivation shows the full sovereign spread rather than one convenient number. BVL is issued by a German federal authority and defines what counts as technically avoidable under Article 17 of EU Regulation 1223/2009, which is binding EU law; it is not a trade-association guideline. The US FDA draft cosmetic lead guidance (10 mg/kg) is gated as draft and is looser in any case.

Cd.label: strictest applicable sovereign finished-cosmetic cadmium limit (Germany BVL 2017 Table 1)
Cd.basis_label: finished cosmetic as placed on market (total content, ug/kg of product as sold)
Cd.substantiation: BVL 2017 sets cadmium at 0.1 mg/kg for cosmetic products in general with NO make-up or theatrical carve-out - the exception list BVL writes for lead and arsenic does not exist for cadmium - so 100 ug/kg binds every row in this category directly, including the decorative ones. It is thirty to fifty times stricter than Health Canada (3 mg/kg), China NMPA (5 mg/kg) and Taiwan MOHW (5 mg/kg), all named for spread.

tAs.label: strictest applicable sovereign finished-cosmetic total-arsenic limit (Germany BVL 2017 Table 1)
tAs.basis_label: finished cosmetic as placed on market (total content, ug/kg of product as sold)
tAs.substantiation: BVL 2017 sets total arsenic at 0.5 mg/kg for cosmetic products in general. Its only exception is theatrical, fan or carnival make-up at 2.5 mg/kg, which does not reach this row. China NMPA (2 mg/kg), Taiwan MOHW (3 mg/kg) and Health Canada (3 mg/kg) are named for spread. Arsenic is reported as TOTAL arsenic; the inorganic species is controlled in its own cell and can never substitute for this one.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction anywhere in the register speciates arsenic in a cosmetic product. Every sovereign cosmetic instrument - Germany BVL 2017, Health Canada, China NMPA 2015, Taiwan MOHW 2024, Korea MFDS, the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive and its national transpositions, India, Kenya, the EAEU - regulates arsenic as a TOTAL element, so there is no sovereign inorganic-arsenic cell for this or any adjacent cosmetic form. Nor is a near-neighbour read-across supportable: the only inorganic-arsenic maximum levels in the register are dietary (rice, fish oils, marine products), expressed on an as-consumed or whole-commodity food basis that is not comparable to a finished-cosmetic total-content basis, and importing one would be exactly the basis conflation this row's basis guard exists to prevent. Inorganic arsenic is nonetheless material rather than not-material in this category: arsenic in talc, mica, zinc oxide, titanium dioxide, iron oxides and clay-derived raw materials is predominantly inorganic, and mineral raw materials are present by design in four of this category's sixteen rows. The cell is therefore a control, not a not-material determination, and inorganic arsenic can never substitute for the total-arsenic cell.
control.reference_method: Speciated inorganic arsenic by HPLC-ICP-MS (EN 16802 or AOAC 2016.03, matrix-validated for the product form) on every certified lot, reported alongside the total-arsenic determination. No separate inorganic-arsenic ceiling is published; the lot is judged against the total-arsenic ceiling, which bounds inorganic arsenic by identity. ESCALATION: where inorganic arsenic is the majority of the reported total arsenic, or where the reported inorganic arsenic is above the manufacturer's trailing twelve-month distribution for the same form, the lot triggers mandatory raw-material traceback to the mineral or botanical component and a documented corrective-action plan before certification.

tHg.label: strictest applicable sovereign finished-cosmetic total-mercury limit (Germany BVL 2017 Table 1)
tHg.basis_label: finished cosmetic as placed on market (total content, ug/kg of product as sold)
tHg.substantiation: BVL 2017 sets mercury at 0.1 mg/kg for cosmetic products in general, ten times stricter than the cluster of sovereigns that all landed on 1 mg/kg: US FDA 21 CFR 700.13 (a binding adulteration rule, not guidance), Health Canada, Hong Kong Cap. 640, China NMPA and Taiwan MOHW. All are named so the record shows that the binding value is the strict tail of a well-populated distribution rather than a lone outlier. Mercury is reported as TOTAL mercury; methylmercury is bounded by this ceiling and is treated in its own cell.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is a component of total mercury and cannot exceed it (MeHg <= tHg by identity), so the binding total-mercury ceiling on this row bounds it arithmetically. Methylmercury is produced by microbial methylation of inorganic mercury in anoxic aquatic and sediment systems and reaches humans by bioaccumulation through aquatic food chains. Neither the pathway nor the exposure route exists here: a finished cosmetic contains no anoxic aquatic compartment and no microbial methylating community, and the product is applied topically rather than eaten. Mercury compounds are prohibited as cosmetic ingredients under EU Regulation 1223/2009 Annex II and are limited only as an unavoidable trace by the instruments named in the total-mercury cell, and every one of those instruments regulates mercury as a total element or as elemental mercury. No separate methylmercury ceiling is published; mercury on this row is governed entirely by the total-mercury cell.
not_material.reference_method: No routine methylmercury determination is required. Total mercury is determined on every certified lot by microwave-assisted acid digestion with ICP-MS or by direct thermal-decomposition amalgamation atomic absorption, and the total-mercury ceiling bounds methylmercury by identity. RE-OPENING RULE: the applicability determination is re-opened, and methylmercury speciation (US EPA 1630 or an equivalent matrix-validated procedure) is performed, whenever the formulation declares a marine-derived raw material - algal or seaweed extract, marine collagen, fish or krill oil, marine-sourced squalane - since that is the only credible route by which organomercury could enter a cosmetic supply chain.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction sets a methylmercury limit for a cosmetic product. Every sovereign cosmetic mercury instrument checked regulates mercury as a total element (or, in the US case, expressly as elemental mercury), because the cosmetic exposure route is dermal with incidental oral transfer and the cosmetic raw-material supply chain contains no organomercury source. The register's only methylmercury maximum levels are dietary limits on predator fish, tuna, shark, marlin, alfonsino and other marine animals, all on a fresh or frozen edible-portion food basis with no comparability to a finished cosmetic.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: Germany BVL 2017 Table 1 (technically avoidable heavy-metal contents in cosmetics); EU Regulation 1223/2009 Annexes II and III; US FDA 21 CFR 700.13; Washington State Toxic-Free Cosmetics Act; Health Canada Guidance on Heavy Metal Impurities in Cosmetics; China NMPA Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics 2015; Korea MFDS cosmetic trace-contaminant standards (2024 Notice No. 9 and the 2025 revision); Taiwan MOHW 2024; Hong Kong Cap. 640; ASEAN Cosmetic Directive 2019 and its Indonesian (BPOM 16/2024), Malaysian (NPRA 2022), Singaporean (HSA 2024) and Thai transpositions; India Cosmetics Rules 2020; Kenya KS 2937:2021; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; Sri Lanka SLS 187:2025 (draft, gated).
not_material.substantiation: Speciation-bounded and matrix-justified. The determination is rebuttable and is re-opened by the marine-raw-material rule in the reference method; it is not a claim that mercury is absent, only that the organomercury species has no formation pathway or supply-chain entry point in this matrix and is bounded by the published total-mercury ceiling.

Ni.label: Korea MFDS cosmetic nickel limit, non-colour-cosmetic tier
Ni.basis_label: finished cosmetic as placed on market (total content, ug/kg of product as sold)
Ni.substantiation: Korea's MFDS is the only sovereign in the register that sets a nickel limit for a finished cosmetic, and it tiers it: 10 ug/g for cosmetics other than eye make-up or colour make-up, 30 ug/g for colour make-up, 35 ug/g for eye make-up. This row is not a colour cosmetic, so the 10 ug/g tier applies directly. Both the 2024 Notice No. 9 row and the 2025 revision row are named; they carry the same value and naming both shows the limit survived a revision cycle. Nickel is a leading contact-sensitiser in children, which is why the cell is published as a firm ceiling rather than a control even though only one jurisdiction sets it.

control.rationale: No sovereign publishes a tin content limit for a finished cosmetic. The register's tin values are of two incompatible kinds. The food maximum levels (canned foods and beverages, 50-250 mg/kg) are dietary as-consumed limits set for tinplate migration into food and have no relationship to a topical product. The EU values are either Toy Safety Directive 2009/48 element-MIGRATION limits, which measure what leaches from an article under simulated mouthing and are numerically incomparable to a total-content number, or REACH entry 20, which caps ORGANOTIN species (dibutyltin and dioctyltin) at 0.1% in skin-contact and childcare articles and is a species limit, not a total-tin ceiling. Substituting any of these would be a basis or species conflation, so no number is published and the cell is a control.
control.reference_method: Total tin by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS on the finished product, every certified lot. Result reported and trended lot over lot. Where the product carries a polymeric applicator, dispensing component or wipe substrate, that component is digested and analysed separately and is additionally screened for dibutyltin and dioctyltin by GC-MS against the EU REACH entry-20 0.1% article limit, which does apply to a skin-contact childcare article as an article limit even though it does not bind the cosmetic formulation. ESCALATION: any lot above the manufacturer's trailing twelve-month distribution for the same form, or any organotin detection on a polymeric component, triggers raw-material traceback and a documented corrective-action plan.

control.rationale: No sovereign publishes an aluminium limit for a finished cosmetic. The only aluminium values in the register are EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48 element-MIGRATION limits, a different basis entirely. The regulatory silence is not an oversight: aluminium is an INTENTIONALLY ADDED functional ingredient across this category - alumina is the standard surface coating on cosmetic-grade titanium dioxide and zinc oxide, aluminium starch octenylsuccinate is a routine powder and emulsion texturiser, and aluminium lakes are the standard insolubilised form of organic colourants - so no jurisdiction treats aluminium as a contaminant to be capped in a cosmetic. Because aluminium is present by design, a not-material determination would be false and an invented ceiling would be arbitrary; the cell is a control.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS on the finished product, every certified lot. The applicant declares the intended functional aluminium contribution from named ingredients and its expected mass fraction; the measured total is reconciled against that declaration. ESCALATION: measured total aluminium materially above the declared functional contribution indicates an undeclared aluminium-bearing raw material or a contaminated mineral input and triggers raw-material traceback, ingredient-declaration review and a documented corrective-action plan before certification.

control.rationale: No sovereign publishes a total-chromium limit for a finished cosmetic. The three total-chromium values in the register (Mexico NOM-252 toy and school-article materials, Australia Customs 1956 toy coatings, ASTM F963 toys and children's articles, all at 60 mg/kg) are bioavailable-soluble MIGRATION limits on articles, not total-content limits on a cosmetic formulation, and reading one across would be the basis conflation this row's guard exists to prevent. Total chromium would in any case be a poor standalone ceiling: chromium in a cosmetic matrix is dominated by trivalent chromium, which is an essential trace element of low toxicity, so a total-chromium number would be non-protective against the species that actually matters. Total chromium is therefore controlled as a screening determination that gates the hexavalent-chromium cell, and no ceiling is published.
control.reference_method: Total chromium by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS on the finished product, every certified lot. Reported as a screening total only and explicitly not as a health-protective ceiling. ESCALATION: any total-chromium result above the matrix-validated method reporting limit triggers mandatory hexavalent-chromium speciation on the same lot under the Cr(VI) cell's method; a total-chromium result above the manufacturer's trailing twelve-month distribution for the same form additionally triggers raw-material traceback to the pigment or mineral component.

control.rationale: No sovereign publishes a hexavalent-chromium limit for a finished cosmetic. The only Cr(VI) value in the cosmetic instrument family is EU REACH Regulation 2020/2081 at 500 ug/kg, which is scoped to mixtures used for TATTOOING AND PERMANENT MAKE-UP - deposited intradermally, bypassing the skin barrier entirely - and is therefore a different exposure route, a different product class and a different risk basis; it is not read across onto a surface-applied children's cosmetic. The remaining Cr(VI) values are EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48 element-migration limits on toy materials, a different basis again. A NOT-MATERIAL determination was considered and rejected for this category. The method-artifact argument - that Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III) in a reducing, organic, aqueous matrix - holds for some cosmetic forms but is not supportable category-wide here: although this row is a predominantly organic, aqueous or oleaginous matrix in which hexavalent chromium would be expected to reduce to trivalent chromium, the reduction rate in a low-water anhydrous or high-pH formulation is not established, mineral-derived fillers and colourants may still be present, and Category 2 is the child-scoped category where an unsubstantiated not-material claim carries the highest cost if it is wrong. Control is the correct fail-safe: testing is mandatory, the method and escalation rule are published, and no ceiling is fabricated.
control.reference_method: Hexavalent chromium by alkaline digestion and ion chromatography with post-column derivatisation (US EPA 3060A with 7199, or an equivalent matrix-validated procedure), performed on every lot whose total-chromium screen is above the method reporting limit, and on every lot of a mineral- or pigment-bearing form regardless of the screen result. ESCALATION: any Cr(VI) detected above the matrix-validated method reporting limit triggers mandatory raw-material traceback to the pigment or mineral component, a supplier certificate of analysis for Cr(VI) on that raw material, and a documented corrective-action plan before the lot may be certified.

tHg.substantiation: BVL 2017 sets mercury at 0.1 mg/kg for cosmetic products in general, ten times stricter than the cluster of sovereigns that all landed on 1 mg/kg: US FDA 21 CFR 700.13 (a binding adulteration rule, not guidance), Health Canada, Hong Kong Cap. 640, China NMPA and Taiwan MOHW. All are named so the record shows that the binding value is the strict tail of a well-populated distribution rather than a lone outlier. Mercury is reported as TOTAL mercury; methylmercury is bounded by this ceiling and is treated in its own cell.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is a component of total mercury and cannot exceed it (MeHg <= tHg by identity), so the binding total-mercury ceiling on this row bounds it arithmetically. Methylmercury is produced by microbial methylation of inorganic mercury in anoxic aquatic and sediment systems and reaches humans by bioaccumulation through aquatic food chains. Neither the pathway nor the exposure route exists here: a finished cosmetic contains no anoxic aquatic compartment and no microbial methylating community, and the product is applied topically rather than eaten. Mercury compounds are prohibited as cosmetic ingredients under EU Regulation 1223/2009 Annex II and are limited only as an unavoidable trace by the instruments named in the total-mercury cell, and every one of those instruments regulates mercury as a total element or as elemental mercury. No separate methylmercury ceiling is published; mercury on this row is governed entirely by the total-mercury cell.
not_material.reference_method: No routine methylmercury determination is required. Total mercury is determined on every certified lot by microwave-assisted acid digestion with ICP-MS or by direct thermal-decomposition amalgamation atomic absorption, and the total-mercury ceiling bounds methylmercury by identity. RE-OPENING RULE: the applicability determination is re-opened, and methylmercury speciation (US EPA 1630 or an equivalent matrix-validated procedure) is performed, whenever the formulation declares a marine-derived raw material - algal or seaweed extract, marine collagen, fish or krill oil, marine-sourced squalane - since that is the only credible route by which organomercury could enter a cosmetic supply chain.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction sets a methylmercury limit for a cosmetic product. Every sovereign cosmetic mercury instrument checked regulates mercury as a total element (or, in the US case, expressly as elemental mercury), because the cosmetic exposure route is dermal with incidental oral transfer and the cosmetic raw-material supply chain contains no organomercury source. The register's only methylmercury maximum levels are dietary limits on predator fish, tuna, shark, marlin, alfonsino and other marine animals, all on a fresh or frozen edible-portion food basis with no comparability to a finished cosmetic.

Ni.label: Korea MFDS cosmetic nickel limit, non-colour-cosmetic tier
Ni.basis_label: finished cosmetic as placed on market (total content, ug/kg of product as sold)
Ni.substantiation: Korea's MFDS is the only sovereign in the register that sets a nickel limit for a finished cosmetic, and it tiers it: 10 ug/g for cosmetics other than eye make-up or colour make-up, 30 ug/g for colour make-up, 35 ug/g for eye make-up. This row is not a colour cosmetic, so the 10 ug/g tier applies directly. Both the 2024 Notice No. 9 row and the 2025 revision row are named; they carry the same value and naming both shows the limit survived a revision cycle. Nickel is a leading contact-sensitiser in children, which is why the cell is published as a firm ceiling rather than a control even though only one jurisdiction sets it.

control.rationale: No sovereign publishes a tin content limit for a finished cosmetic. The register's tin values are of two incompatible kinds. The food maximum levels (canned foods and beverages, 50-250 mg/kg) are dietary as-consumed limits set for tinplate migration into food and have no relationship to a topical product. The EU values are either Toy Safety Directive 2009/48 element-MIGRATION limits, which measure what leaches from an article under simulated mouthing and are numerically incomparable to a total-content number, or REACH entry 20, which caps ORGANOTIN species (dibutyltin and dioctyltin) at 0.1% in skin-contact and childcare articles and is a species limit, not a total-tin ceiling. Substituting any of these would be a basis or species conflation, so no number is published and the cell is a control.

Where the product carries a polymeric applicator, dispensing component or wipe substrate, that component is digested and analysed separately and is additionally screened for dibutyltin and dioctyltin by GC-MS against the EU REACH entry-20 0.1% article limit, which does apply to a skin-contact childcare article as an article limit even though it does not bind the cosmetic formulation. ESCALATION: any lot above the manufacturer's trailing twelve-month distribution for the same form, or any organotin detection on a polymeric component, triggers raw-material traceback and a documented corrective-action plan.

control.rationale: No sovereign publishes an aluminium limit for a finished cosmetic. The only aluminium values in the register are EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48 element-MIGRATION limits, a different basis entirely. The regulatory silence is not an oversight: aluminium is an INTENTIONALLY ADDED functional ingredient across this category - alumina is the standard surface coating on cosmetic-grade titanium dioxide and zinc oxide, aluminium starch octenylsuccinate is a routine powder and emulsion texturiser, and aluminium lakes are the standard insolubilised form of organic colourants - so no jurisdiction treats aluminium as a contaminant to be capped in a cosmetic. Because aluminium is present by design, a not-material determination would be false and an invented ceiling would be arbitrary; the cell is a control.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS on the finished product, every certified lot. The applicant declares the intended functional aluminium contribution from named ingredients and its expected mass fraction; the measured total is reconciled against that declaration. ESCALATION: measured total aluminium materially above the declared functional contribution indicates an undeclared aluminium-bearing raw material or a contaminated mineral input and triggers raw-material traceback, ingredient-declaration review and a documented corrective-action plan before certification.

control.rationale: No sovereign publishes a total-chromium limit for a finished cosmetic. control.rationale: No sovereign publishes a hexavalent-chromium limit for a finished cosmetic. control.reference_method: Hexavalent chromium by alkaline digestion and ion chromatography with post-column derivatisation (US EPA 3060A with 7199, or an equivalent matrix-validated procedure), performed on every lot whose total-chromium screen is above the method reporting limit, and on every lot of a mineral- or pigment-bearing form regardless of the screen result. ESCALATION: any Cr(VI) detected above the matrix-validated method reporting limit triggers mandatory raw-material traceback to the pigment or mineral component, a supplier certificate of analysis for Cr(VI) on that raw material, and a documented corrective-action plan before the lot may be certified.

baby-powder-cornstarch.name: Baby powder, cornstarch base (clean counterpart)

This is the mineral-bearing counterpart of the cornstarch row and is the highest-metal-load form in the category: talc is a mined magnesium silicate whose deposits are geologically co-located with metal-bearing ore, and the finished product is essentially undiluted mineral. What this row adds over the cornstarch row is not a different number but a raw-material qualification obligation: the talc or silicate lot is qualified at the mine or supplier level with a certificate of analysis covering the full panel before the finished product is tested. Asbestiform amphibole contamination of cosmetic talc is a serious and separate hazard; it is not a heavy metal and is out of scope for this contract, and nothing in this standard should be read as addressing it.

control.reference_method: Hexavalent chromium by alkaline digestion and ion chromatography with post-column derivatisation (US EPA 3060A with 7199, or an equivalent matrix-validated procedure), performed on every lot whose total-chromium screen is above the method reporting limit, and on every lot of a mineral- or pigment-bearing form regardless of the screen result. ESCALATION: any Cr(VI) detected above the matrix-validated method reporting limit triggers mandatory raw-material traceback to the pigment or mineral component, a supplier certificate of analysis for Cr(VI) on that raw material, and a documented corrective-action plan before the lot may be certified.
